newsitem.title: UK: Actuaries say end of ACT credit to hit UK pensions.
newsitem.headline: Actuaries say end of ACT credit to hit UK pensions.

text.p: The British government has under-estimated the adverse impact of abolishing the Advanced Corporation Tax (ACT) credit on pension scheme members and plan holders, according to the Association of Consulting Actuaries(ACA).
"Abolishing the ACT credit will cut by 20 percent the income from UK equities, which typically form 60 percent of fund assets," the ACA said in a statement.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown announced in his Wednesday budget speech the abolition of the ACT credit, which allows pension funds to claim a rebate on ACT.

"Abolishing the ACT credit will inevitably mean good occupational schemes will be abolished by some companies, particularly smaller concerns already struggling with the added regulatory costs recently imposed by the Pensions Act," the statement said.
